nodes.title: Prompt Template
widgets_values:
Analyze only the visible face and head.

Describe only the most important visible identity traits.

For humans, include:

* apparent gender
* approximate age
* skin tone
* eye color
* hair color
* basic hairstyle
* one distinctive facial feature only if clearly relevant

Do not mention absent features such as "no facial hair".
Do not describe clothing, body, pose, expression, background, lighting, camera, or minor facial anatomy.

For non-human subjects, briefly state the subject type and only the most important visible head traits.

Keep the description very short, approximately 8–20 words.

OUTPUT EXACTLY ONCE.

Use exactly this structure:

head_swap:
FACE: <one short English sentence>

Never repeat the output.
Never generate a second head_swap block.
Never generate a second FACE block.
Never provide multiple candidates or alternatives.
Do not add blank lines.
Do not add explanations or extra text.
Immediately stop generating after the period at the end of line 3.

Example:

head_swap:
FACE:
Female, pale skin, approximately 20–30 years old, red eyes, long black hair.

nodes.title: Note: About LTX-2.5
widgets_values:
# LTX-2.5

LTX-2.5 is Lightricks' open video generation model : fast, local-first, and built for production. Run it locally, fine-tune it for your own use case, or integrate it into your pipeline.

**Key highlights:**

- **Pixel Diffusion** : keyframes-first generation that builds every scene on a grid of high-fidelity keyframes for industry-leading pixel quality
- **Diffusion Video Decoder** : sharper faces, legible text, fewer smears in fast motion
- **Native multishot** : one generation yields multiple connected shots holding character, environment, lighting, voice, and style across cuts
- **Custom Gemma 4 12B text encoder** : retains multiple subjects, actions, lighting, detail, and camera direction across complex prompts
- **Dedicated Prompt Enhancer** : a lightweight model that expands short prompts into rich cinematic instructions at near-zero extra compute
- **Auto Duration** : predicts the right clip length from the described action before diffusion begins
- **Better distilled model** : carries far more quality, prompt adherence, and motion into a smaller, faster variant
- Carried over from LTX-2.3: native 4K, synchronized audio-video

Official model & files: https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5
## What this workflow does

This **Image-to-Video** workflow animates a first frame into a video. Load a starting image, describe the motion in the prompt, and the model continues the scene while holding character, lighting, and style : with synchronized audio.

## Subgraph parameters

The **Image to Video (LTX-2.5)** node is a subgraph. Click the **Enter subgraph** button at the bottom of the node to open its internal graph, where you can inspect and fine-tune every step of the pipeline (conditioning, sampler, CFG guider, VAE decode, and more).

| Parameter | What it does |
|---|---|
| first_frame | Starting image that the video continues from (load your own image in **Load First Frame**) |
| prompt | Text prompt describing the motion, scene, lighting, camera, and style |
| prompt_enhance | Toggle the built-in Prompt Enhancer: expands short prompts into rich cinematic instructions at near-zero extra compute |
| duration | Clip length in seconds (Auto Duration can predict it from the action) |
| width / height | Output resolution in pixels (e.g. 1280×720) |
| seed | Random seed : set a fixed value to reproduce the same result |
| frame_rate | Frames per second |
| unet_name | Main model: LTX-2.5 distilled transformer (ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors) |
| video_vae | Video VAE used for decoding (ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors) |
| audio_vae | Audio VAE that produces synchronized audio (ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors) |
| clip_name | Text encoder: custom Gemma 4 12B with projection (gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors) |
| upscale_model | Latent upscaler applied before decoding for higher-fidelity output |
| prompt_enhance_model | Model checkpoint used by the Prompt Enhancer |

## How to use

1. Download the models listed in **Note: Model Links** and place them in ComfyUI's `models/` folder
2. Replace the image in **Load First Frame** with your own starting frame
3. Write a prompt describing the motion, optionally toggle **prompt_enhance** for short prompts
4. Set **duration** / **width** / **height** / **frame_rate** (defaults work well) and hit **Queue**
5. To dive deeper, click **Enter subgraph** at the bottom of the main node : every internal step (conditioning, sampler, CFG, VAE decode) can be edited there

nodes.title: Face Reference (close-up shot for greater fidelity)

widgets_values: The second pass might alter the face, because I'm using the reference guide again instead of the result from the first step. To avoid making too many changes and only improve the quality, the denoise is at 0.1. If you increase it more than that, the difference will be greater, but there may be other ways to improve it that I haven't explored yet.
